name: MLAgentBench
summary: Evaluates agents that read and modify files, run experiments, and inspect results across 13 machine-learning tasks, from CIFAR-10 improvement to BabyLM. Task success exposes planning and experimentation failures within supplied problems; it does not measure autonomous selection of important research questions or independently validated scientific discoveries.

name: MLE-bench
summary: Packages 75 Kaggle competitions to assess dataset preparation, model training, and iterative experimentation, with historical leaderboard thresholds as reference points. Useful for engineering-focused research agents and resource-scaling studies. A competition medal measures predictive performance under a particular setup; it is not evidence of novel hypotheses or scientific validity beyond that task.

name: RE-Bench
summary: Compares agents with human experts on seven open-ended machine-learning research engineering environments, including optimization tasks with executable scoring functions. Its human-attempt data and multiple time budgets make resource assumptions visible. Results concern bounded AI research engineering, and rankings can change with time allowance; they do not establish general scientific autonomy.

name: PaperBench
summary: Asks agents to implement and execute replications of 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch. Author-developed hierarchical rubrics divide the work into 8,316 gradable items, with a separately assessed model-based grader. Scores indicate progress toward specified replication requirements; code-only variants, partial rubric credit, and successful empirical replication must be distinguished.

name: ScienceAgentBench
summary: Contains 102 expert-validated tasks derived from 44 publications across four disciplines. Each task requires a self-contained Python program, assessed through code, execution outputs, and costs. The benchmark deliberately tests individual data-driven research steps, providing a stronger basis for bounded capability claims than treating generated manuscripts as evidence of complete scientific discovery.

name: DiscoveryBench
summary: Tests hypothesis discovery from supplied datasets, metadata, and natural-language goals using 264 literature-derived tasks across six domains, plus 903 synthetic tasks. Facet-based evaluation separates aspects of a proposed finding. The target is recovering supported relationships within provided data, with synthetic and real tasks reported separately, rather than discovering unrestricted new scientific knowledge.

name: SciCode
summary: Uses 80 scientist-authored research coding problems, decomposed into 338 subproblems across 16 subfields, to test scientific knowledge and executable implementation. Report main-problem and subproblem accuracy separately, including whether background information was supplied. This assesses specified computational tasks; the later SciCode-Verified audit also makes benchmark version and test defects relevant to comparisons.

name: MLRC-Bench
summary: Evaluates proposing and implementing methods for seven challenging machine-learning research competitions using objective task metrics and constrained evaluation protocols. It directly examines the gap between judge-rated innovation and measured performance. The competition setting supports claims about research-method execution and improvement over baselines, while broader scientific importance remains outside its scoring procedure.

name: CORE-Bench
summary: Measures computational reproducibility using supplied code and data: 270 tasks from 90 papers across computer science, social science, and medicine, with three difficulty levels. Agents must recover results and answer questions about them. Re-running artifacts does not validate the underlying scientific claims; the 2026 follow-up introduces v1.1 and out-of-distribution tasks after auditing shortcuts.

name: BixBench
summary: Evaluates bioinformatics agents on more than 50 practical analysis scenarios with nearly 300 associated questions. Tasks require exploring biological datasets, performing multistep analyses, and interpreting results. Open-answer and multiple-choice settings test different behaviors; correctness on these prepared analyses should not be presented as validation of new biological mechanisms or experimental discoveries.

name: Scientist-Bench
summary: Introduced with AI-Researcher, this benchmark derives guided innovation and open-ended exploration tasks from AI research papers, supplying references, instructions, and datasets. The initial paper evaluates 22 reference papers and six open-ended tasks. Implementation assessments and comparative manuscript judgments cover several workflow stages, but judge-rated similarity to human research is not independent confirmation of novel scientific findings.

name: SciReplicate-Bench
summary: Assesses algorithm comprehension and implementation through 100 tasks extracted from 36 NLP papers published in 2024. Evaluation combines executable tests, reasoning-graph comparison, and repository dependency or API measures. Its scope is reproducing selected algorithmic components from papers; passing those tasks does not imply that every experiment or headline paper result was replicated.

name: LAB-Bench
summary: Provides more than 2,400 multiple-choice questions targeting practical biology-research capabilities, including literature reasoning, figure interpretation, database navigation, and sequence manipulation. Expert comparisons help contextualize performance on research-adjacent tasks. These are bounded question-answer evaluations, so high scores alone do not demonstrate reliable laboratory execution, end-to-end biological research, or novel experimental validation.

name: ScienceBoard
summary: Places agents in scientific software environments and evaluates 169 tasks across six domains through graphical, command-line, or mixed interactions. Programmatic checks assess outcomes in applications used for activities such as molecular analysis and geospatial work. It tests practical computer-use workflows; completing these tasks is narrower than independently conducting a sustained research program.

name: AI Idea Bench 2025
summary: Evaluates AI research idea generation using 3,495 target papers and their motivating references. Its protocol compares generated ideas with paper content and reference-based judgments, including novelty and feasibility assessments. Historical alignment provides a repeatable proxy for ideation quality, but resemblance to published work cannot establish prospective novelty, successful execution, or future scientific impact.

name: RINoBench
summary: Tests research-idea novelty judgments with 1,381 expert-derived ideas and nine metrics covering numerical novelty ratings and written justifications. The authors find that human-like explanations can coexist with inaccurate novelty judgments. This is useful for evaluating critic or reviewer agents, while novelty-rating agreement remains distinct from feasibility, empirical correctness, and discovery value.

name: IdeaForecastBench
summary: Evaluates whether ideas proposed from literature available before a cutoff correspond to later publications. It contains 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics, generates up to five ranked ideas, and reports separate judge results. This measures research forecasting under a retrospective protocol; broad or generic predictions and judge sensitivity complicate interpretation as precise scientific anticipation.
status: The arXiv record reports acceptance to EMNLP 2026; a proceedings record was not located during this check.

name: FrontierScience
summary: Assesses expert-level physics, chemistry, and biology reasoning using Olympiad and Research splits. The released gold sets contain 100 short-answer questions and 60 research subtasks, with model grading against answers or rubrics. These constrained, expert-authored tasks probe scientific reasoning; the creators explicitly distinguish them from the broader work of producing new discoveries.

name: SEER-Repro
summary: Evaluates reproduction of 2,190 atomic claims from 20 published SEER-based studies using database documentation and executable analyses. Numerical tolerances and model-assisted evidence grading determine claim outcomes. Scores concern the selected papers and available registry release; matching reported claims does not establish robustness to alternative analyses or independent verification of all code.
status: Benchmark described in the preprint; a public code and benchmark-package release was not verified in the inspected sources.

name: SciPIvot
summary: Tests scientific judgment through 248 decisions drawn from human corrections across 26 research projects. Models choose between an original agent plan and a human-corrected alternative, with or without the prior project record. This evaluates recognition of selected corrective decisions, not plan generation, research execution, or the prevalence of failures across scientific work.

name: PhysClosureBench
summary: Provides 50 physics research tasks with specified goals and constraints. A 20-criterion score measures local accomplishments, while a separate closure assessment tests whether essential evidence and applicability conditions resolve the research question. Model-based grading includes a selected human consistency check; high partial scores are not equivalent to complete scientific closure.
status: Execution framework and Case 30 example are public; the author-linked Hugging Face page provides the 50-case materials. Scientific grading is separate from the execution harness.

name: AInsteinBench
summary: Evaluates scientific software development using tasks derived from maintainer pull requests across six research codebases. Executable tests assess changes in domains including chemistry, molecular dynamics, and numerical relativity. This measures repository-level implementation and verification under specified tests; it does not assess autonomous hypothesis selection or establish correctness beyond the tested behavior.
status: Public evaluation code and question files; the README states that Docker images for Multi-SWE-bench-format questions are available upon request.
